title: Image Processing
prompt:
Write a program that uses a for loop to apply a filter to an image.
Sample Input: image.jpg
Sample Output: filtered_image.jpg
answer:
Sure, I can help you with that. Here's an example Python program that uses the OpenCV library to apply a Gaussian blur filter to an image using a for loop. Before running the code, make sure you have installed the OpenCV library by following the instructions in the OpenCV documentation: <https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d7/d6f/tutorial_py_install.html>

```python
import cv2

# Replace this with the path to your image
image_path = "image.jpg"

# Load the image
image = cv2.imread(image_path)

# Apply Gaussian blur filter using a for loop
kernel_size = 5  # Adjust the kernel size as needed
for i in range(image.shape[0]):
    for j in range(image.shape[1]):
        # Get the pixel value at the current position
        pixel = image[i, j]

        # Apply Gaussian blur using the specified kernel size
        blurred_pixel = cv2.GaussianBlur(pixel, (kernel_size, kernel_size), 0)

        # Set the pixel value to the blurred value
        image[i, j] = blurred_pixel

# Save the filtered image
cv2.imwrite("filtered_image.jpg", image)
```

This program reads the image, applies a Gaussian blur filter to each pixel using a for loop, and then saves the filtered image to a new file named `filtered_image.jpg`. You can adjust the `kernel_size` variable to change the amount of blur applied to the image.
